outcome: Gestational hypertension with or without preeclampsia
cohort: 11,136 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies at more than 28 gestational weeks in Beijing, China
finding: The risks of gestational hypertension with or without preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, initial cesarean section, postpartum hemorrhage, macrosomia, and large-for-gestational age infants were increased in women with higher pre-pregnancy BMI, while lower pre-pregnancy BMI was associated with increased risk of small-for-gestational age infants.
mod_finding: This study found that women with higher pre-pregnancy BMI had increased odds of initial cesarean section.
